$comment: Version/source matrix for third-party libraries under compile/lib*. Extracted from the Dockerfiles on 2026-09-11 (see CLAUDE.md, decision 11). 'latest' in config.yaml resolves to the last entry of 'versions'. GitHub-hosted libraries (sourceType github-release/github-tag) are auto-refreshed via `node compile/cli.mjs update-versions` (compile/update-lib-versions.mjs); everything else (tarball/sourceforge/googlesource sources) still has to be checked manually via its own checkUrl.

libcurl.note: GitHub release tags use underscores (e.g. curl-8_22_0) rather than dots; update-lib-versions.mjs normalizes them to dots before recording here. TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: 8.22.0 builds cleanly once `--without-libpsl` is added to compile/libcurl/Dockerfile's configure flags — curl 8.x added a hard `libpsl` (Public Suffix List, cookie-domain-matching) dependency we don't vendor; disabling that optional feature is enough (HTTP2/nghttp2 support confirmed still enabled in the build log). compile/Makefile's CURL_VERSION now reads this array's last entry directly (see CLAUDE.md decision 27) rather than being hand-synced.

libzip.note: Two versions are built in parallel by the Makefile (1.2.0 and 1.9.2), not a single 'latest' — hardcoded directly in compile/Makefile's libzip_jspi/LIBZIP_VERSION build args, NOT read from this array at all, unlike every other library here. autoUpdate:false because update-lib-versions.mjs writing a new 'latest' here would be a no-op at best (the Makefile ignores it) and misleading at worst. Checked 2026-09-17: upstream's current release is 1.11.4 — not adopted, since bumping either pinned version means editing the Makefile by hand and re-testing both builds.

libopenssl.note: Upstream Playground pinned two versions built in parallel (1.1.0h/1.1.1t) for broader PHP-version support; we only target PHP 8.5 (see CLAUDE.md decision 16) so compile/Makefile now builds a single version. Verified 2026-09-12 that 3.6.4 (latest stable 3.x; 4.0.x exists but is very new) cross-compiles with the existing Dockerfile unmodified. autoUpdate:false because 'latest' here means 'latest patch on our chosen 3.x line', a judgment call update-lib-versions.mjs shouldn't make on its own (it would happily jump to 4.x once that's what openssl-library.org calls current). Re-checked 2026-09-17: still no newer 3.6.x patch than 3.6.4; 4.0 exists but isn't being adopted yet.

libImageMagick.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest version first, only fall back to an older pin if it actually fails a real test build. TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: 7.1.2-31 rebuilds cleanly against the fresh libpng16/libjpeg/libwebp below.

libiconv.note: Checked 2026-09-17: 1.19 is latest (tarball URL confirmed resolving), added — not yet build-tested against this pipeline.

libjpeg.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest version first. update-lib-versions.mjs's github-tag fallback is noisy for this repo (its tags mix in historical IJG libjpeg versions like 'jpeg-9') — 3.2.0 confirmed as latest via the GitHub Releases page directly. TESTED and REVERTED 2026-09-12: 3.2.0 fails a real build — it added a bundled `src/spng/` (PNG) module that uses raw x86 SSE2 intrinsics (`__m128i`, `_mm_cvtsi128_si32`) unconditionally reachable under our `-D__x86_64__` compile flag, which don't exist under Emscripten without `-msimd128`. Stayed on 3.0.3. Would need a real patch (disable spng, or add SIMD polyfill flags) to move forward — not attempted. IMPORTANT: 3.2.0 is deliberately NOT last in `versions` (out of chronological order) — since decision 28 wired compile/Makefile's LIBJPEG_VERSION to `MATRIX_VERSION` (the array's last entry), putting the known-broken version last would make the very next `make libjpeg_jspi` try to build it. Re-checked 2026-09-16 via `update-lib-versions.mjs`: GitHub's real latest release is still 3.2.0 (no newer fix upstream) — the script itself used to report this as a misleading `3.0.3 → 3.2.0` "update" every time, since it only compared against the array's *last* entry rather than checking whether the version was already recorded elsewhere; fixed the script to recognize 3.2.0 is already present and stay silent instead.

libavif.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest version first. TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: v1.4.2 rebuilds cleanly.

libaom.note: Checked 2026-09-17: v3.15.0 is latest stable tag (v3.15.0-rc1 and older rc tags excluded), archive URL confirmed resolving, added — not yet build-tested against this pipeline.

libpng16.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest STABLE version first (github.com/pnggroup/libpng's newest tags are 1.7.0 betas — not stable; 1.6.58 is the latest stable 1.6.x). TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: 1.6.58 rebuilds cleanly.

libxml2.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest version first. TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: v2.15.4 rebuilds cleanly.

libwebp.note: Default policy (2026-09-12): always try the latest version first. TESTED and ADOPTED 2026-09-12: moved off the commit pin to the v1.6.0 tag, rebuilds cleanly (libsharpyuv.a still produced alongside libwebp.a).

libsqlite3.note: Checked 2026-09-17: 3.53.4 is latest (sqlite-autoconf-3530400.tar.gz), added — not yet build-tested against this pipeline. sqlite.org's download path is keyed by release YEAR, not derivable from the version number; 3.53.4 lives under /2026/, not /2025/ like the previously-pinned 3.51.0 — both this sourceTemplate and compile/libsqlite3/Dockerfile's hardcoded URL were updated to match. Re-check the year again on the next bump.

libz.note: Checked 2026-09-17: 1.3.2 is latest stable (released 2026-02-17), tarball URL confirmed resolving under the existing /fossils/ path — added, not yet build-tested against this pipeline. A 1.2.13 → 1.3.2 minor bump; zlib's changelog describes it as compatible, but hasn't been verified against this specific cross-compile.

oniguruma.note: NO pinned version in the current Dockerfile: clones the default branch on every build. Reproducibility not guaranteed. Fix by pinning a tag here.

libssh2.$comment: For curl SFTP/SCP support (CLAUDE.md decision 24). Real GitHub org/repo verified via `gh api`, not guessed from memory.

nghttp2.$comment: For curl HTTP/2 support (CLAUDE.md decision 25). Built with --enable-lib-only to skip the CLI apps/examples, which pull in unrelated deps (libcurl, libev, jansson, boost...).

freetype.$comment: GD's FreeType dependency for text rendering (imagettftext/gdImageStringFT). Moved here from plannedLibraries 2026-09-12 once compile/libfreetype/Dockerfile was written and wired into compile/libgd/Dockerfile + compile/php/Dockerfile's WITH_GD block. Tag format is VER-<version with dots replaced by dashes>, e.g. 2.14.3 -> VER-2-14-3; the Dockerfile does that substitution itself.
freetype.note: Bug found and fixed 2026-09-16: update-lib-versions.mjs's github-tag lookup only ever matched plain dotted version tags, so it couldn't resolve anything here at all ("could not resolve a version") — freetype's own VER-2-14-3 dashed tag convention never matched. Fixed the script to convert VER-<N>-<N>-<N> tags to dotted form before filtering/comparing, same as it already did for ImageMagick's own non-standard tag suffix. Re-checked afterward: 2.14.3 is confirmed still latest upstream.

libsodium.$comment: For ext/sodium (CLAUDE.md decision 32 — the mode:shared pilot). Moved here from plannedLibraries 2026-09-12 once compile/libsodium/Dockerfile was written. No dependency on libz/libopenssl — self-contained crypto.

libyaml.$comment: For ext/yaml (CLAUDE.md decision 34, static build). Moved here from plannedLibraries 2026-09-12 once compile/libyaml/Dockerfile was written. Latest tag (0.2.6-rc.1) is a release candidate — pinned to the latest STABLE release instead, same policy as libpng16.

libcmark-gfm.$comment: GitHub's own CommonMark+GFM C library (github/cmark-gfm), for the new ext/mdhtml (CLAUDE.md decision 37, static build) -- the Kirigami markdown extension that replaces ext/cmark, which was tried both statically (decision 35) and as a mode:shared package (decision 38) before being dropped entirely (decision 40). Builds two static archives from one source tree, libcmark-gfm.a (core) and libcmark-gfm-extensions.a (table/strikethrough/autolink/tagfilter/tasklist), see compile/libcmark-gfm/Dockerfile.
libcmark-gfm.note: Real bug found and fixed 2026-09-16, before it could cause damage: update-lib-versions.mjs's normalizeVersion() stripped a tag at its first non-numeric segment, so cmark-gfm's own '0.29.0.gfm.13' tag was silently truncated to '0.29.0' -- not a real, independent cmark-gfm release, just the mangled remainder of the actual one. Writing that would have regressed compile/libcmark-gfm/Dockerfile's resolved version. Fixed the regex to also capture a trailing '.gfm.N' suffix. Re-checked afterward: 0.29.0.gfm.13 is confirmed still latest upstream.

libbz2.$comment: For ext/bz2 (mode: static, added 2026-09-17 so phar gets .tar.bz2 archive support -- see config.yaml's own bz2 note). First tried as a mode:shared vendored-C-library pilot in the same spirit as libsodium/decision 32, but the user's call was to keep bz2 static-only once phar's own dependency on it surfaced (registering the same extension both statically and as a separate shared package would be redundant). Upstream bzip2/libbzip2 has had no release since 1.0.8 (2019); its original maintainer's sourceware.org host is still the canonical distribution point (confirmed via a real directory listing, not assumed) -- no GitHub release/tag exists to source from instead. Keyed 'libbz2' (not 'libbzip2', the upstream project's own name) so compile/Makefile's MATRIX_VERSION lookup and compile/php/Dockerfile's COPY .../libbz2 stay consistent with the compile/libbz2/ directory name.

libgmp.$comment: For ext/gmp (mode: static, next batch after bz2 -- CLAUDE.md decision 53's follow-up, 2026-09-17). GNU MP, the arbitrary-precision arithmetic library ext/gmp's config.m4 requires (gmp.h + __gmpz_rootrem symbol, >= 4.2). Autotools-based like libsodium/libssh2, see compile/libgmp/Dockerfile.

libtidy.$comment: For ext/tidy (mode: static, next batch after bz2 -- CLAUDE.md decision 53's follow-up, 2026-09-17). HTML Tidy (htacg/tidy-html5, the tidy-html5 fork ext/tidy's config.m4 targets via its tidybuffio.h check), CMake-based like libaom, see compile/libtidy/Dockerfile. Keyed 'libtidy' (not 'tidy-html5', the upstream repo name) for the same COPY/Makefile-target consistency reason as libbz2/libbzip2.

libpq.$comment: For ext/pgsql, ext/pdo_pgsql (both mode: shared, 2026-09-22). Moved here from plannedLibraries once compile/libpq/Dockerfile was written and test-built. postgresql/postgres is not a real GitHub org (verified 404) -- PostgreSQL's source releases live at postgresql.org, not vendored on GitHub the same way. Full server source tarball (there's no separate libpq-only release), autotools-based; configure needs --with-template=linux (its own platform-detection has no 'emscripten' entry -- unlike GMP's generic-C fallback for an unrecognized CPU, this is a hard error without it) and --without-icu (default since PG16, and this repo deliberately doesn't vendor ICU -- see config.yaml's intl note). Only the static lib is built (`all-static-lib`/`install-lib-static` Makefile.shlib targets, not the default `all`/`install`, which also build a .so -- that link fails under wasm-ld, "unknown argument: --enable-new-dtags", from Makefile.shlib's own rpath flags on the linux template). No SSL support yet (--without-openssl) -- a possible follow-up, same as mysqlnd's own SSL addition (decision 45's follow-up). Also vendors libpgport_shlib.a/libpgcommon_shlib.a alongside libpq.a itself -- libpq.a alone isn't self-contained (configure's own VAL_LIBS metadata says a static -lpq also needs -lpgcommon -lpgport -lm), confirmed by a genuinely missing pg_vsnprintf symbol at PHP runtime before these were added. See compile/extensions/pgsql/PROVENANCE.md for this and the ac_cv_lib_pq_* config.yaml overrides needed to work around AC_CHECK_LIB being unreliable (false positives) in this side-module WASM linking environment.

openldap.$comment: For ext/ldap (mode: shared, 2026-09-22). Moved here from plannedLibraries once compile/openldap/Dockerfile was written and test-built. GitHub mirror (openldap/openldap) has no releases and non-numeric tags (development branch names) -- openldap.org's own release directory is the real source. Client libraries only (--disable-slapd, no standalone LDAP server built) and dependency-free for a first pass (--without-cyrus-sasl, --without-tls -- SASL is opt-in on the ext/ldap side too, --with-ldap-sasl defaults to off; TLS is a possible follow-up, same shape as mysqlnd's own SSL addition, decision 45's follow-up). Needs --with-yielding_select=yes explicitly (configure can't probe this cross-compiling: "error: crossing compiling: use --with-yielding_select=yes|no|manual"). Only liblutil.a/liblber.la/libldap.la are built, by explicit target name (not the default `make -C libraries`/`make` "all" targets) -- both liblber's and libldap's own default targets also build a diagnostic-only test binary (dtest, apitest) that fails outright under this toolchain (both link liblber.a in twice, once via a relative path and once absolute, and Emscripten's SIDE_MODULE linking wraps every static archive in --whole-archive, so the same archive linked in twice is a duplicate-symbol error). include/ldap_config.h (needed transitively by openldap's own .c files, generated from config.status as part of the top-level "make depend", not by ./configure directly) means `make depend` must run at the top level first, not scoped to libraries/ -- real failure without this: "fatal error: 'ldap_config.h' file not found".

libffi.$comment: For ext/ffi (mode: shared, 2026-09-23) and GLib's own GObject closures (for ext/enchant, mode: shared, 2026-09-22). Moved here from plannedLibraries once compile/libffi/Dockerfile was written and test-built -- straightforward autotools build, no cross-compile surprises.

libglib.$comment: For ext/enchant (mode: shared, 2026-09-22). Moved here from plannedLibraries once compile/libglib/Dockerfile was written and test-built. Keyed 'libglib' (not 'glib', GNOME's own project name) for the same COPY/Makefile-target consistency reason as libbz2/libbzip2. 2.58.x is the LAST autotools-buildable glib series -- 2.60+ is meson-only, which this pipeline has no cross-compilation support for (every other vendored lib is autotools/CMake/plain-Makefile). Deliberately pinned well below 'latest' upstream glib for this reason; do not bump past 2.58.x without first adding real meson cross-compilation support. ext/enchant only needs an older enchant release requiring glib-2.0 + gmodule-2.0 (see compile/extensions/enchant/PROVENANCE.md) -- comfortably within 2.58's feature set despite being 7+ years old. Release tarball ships only configure.ac (no pre-generated ./configure) -- needs autoreconf (via glib's own autogen.sh, which also stubs out gtk-doc.make since gtk-doc isn't installed). Depends on libz (already vendored) and libffi (also newly vendored here, needed unconditionally for GObject's closure marshaling even though ext/enchant itself never touches gobject-2.0).

libenchant2.$comment: For ext/enchant (mode: shared, 2026-09-22). Moved here from plannedLibraries once compile/libenchant2/Dockerfile was written and test-built -- version deliberately DROPPED from the planned 'latest' (2.8.21) to 2.6.9: 2.7.0+ requires gobject-2.0/gio-2.0 (not vendored, see libglib's own note) and 2.8.x's own floor jumped all the way to glib >= 2.76 (meson-only). 2.6.9 is the last release needing only glib-2.0 >= 2.6 + gmodule-2.0, comfortably within vendored glib 2.58.3 -- do not bump without first re-checking configure.ac's own PKG_CHECK_MODULES(GLIB, ...) line for a raised floor. 2.8.21 is deliberately NOT last in `versions` (same convention as libjpeg's 3.2.0): it records upstream's latest as known-but-not-adopted, so update-lib-versions.mjs stays silent instead of proposing it, and MATRIX_VERSION (the last entry) keeps building 2.6.9. No spell-checking provider vendored yet (no hunspell/aspell) -- configure warns ("No spell-checking provider selected!") but does not fail, so dictionaries just won't resolve to anything until a real provider is added as a follow-up. Real libenchant-2.la lives in src/ (not lib/, which only builds a Gnulib portability shim, libgnu.la, a real prerequisite built first) -- targeted by explicit name to avoid src/'s own default target, which also builds two real CLI tools (enchant-2.1, enchant-lsmod-2.1) that hit the same --whole-archive duplicate-symbol failure as openldap's apitest/dtest and glib's gobject-query (each links libenchant in twice, once via a relative path and once absolute). This vendored package also bundles libglib-2.0.a/libgmodule-2.0.a/libffi.a/libz.a alongside libenchant-2.a itself (same 'one self-contained vendorLib' pattern as libpq's own libpgport_shlib.a/libpgcommon_shlib.a) -- ext/enchant's config.m4 has only one PKG_CHECK_MODULES call to override, so all four transitive dependencies need to already be in the same vendored archive set cli.mjs's vendorLibFlags() picks up automatically.

unixodbc.$comment: For ext/odbc (mode: shared, 2026-09-22). unixODBC driver manager only (libodbc.a, which already embeds libodbcinst) -- no bundled drivers (--enable-drivers stays off). Also used by ext/pdo_odbc. See compile/unixodbc/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/odbc/PROVENANCE.md.

freetds.$comment: For ext/pdo_dblib (mode: shared, 2026-09-23). db-lib (libsybdb) only -- no ODBC driver, apps, server or pool; no TLS (so no Azure SQL yet), no Kerberos; charset conversion through musl's iconv. freetds.org's stable/ directory is the real release source (GitHub releases lag behind: 1.5.16 there vs 1.5.19 here). See compile/freetds/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/pdo_dblib/PROVENANCE.md.

firebird.$comment: For ext/pdo_firebird (mode: shared, 2026-09-23). Firebird's client library only (libfbclient: yvalve + remote client + common), built from the full server source release with --enable-client-only, plus its bundled static dependencies (libtommath, libtomcrypt, decNumber, re2). ICU headers are needed to compile but ICU itself is never linked (loaded with dlopen() at runtime, only for charset/collation work). Version includes Firebird's build number (the source tarball is Firebird-<version>-0-source.tar.xz, the release tag v<first three components>), which update-lib-versions.mjs's single-{version} templates can't express -- hence autoUpdate: false; check https://github.com/FirebirdSQL/firebird/releases by hand. See compile/firebird/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/pdo_firebird/PROVENANCE.md.

libxslt.$comment: For ext/xsl (mode: shared, 2026-09-23). Moved here from plannedLibraries. libxslt + libexslt (the same tarball), built against the vendored libxml2 (compile/libxml2, 2.15.4; libxslt 1.1.45 requires >= 2.15.1). No Python bindings, no libgcrypt (EXSLT crypto functions off), no debugger. download.gnome.org is the real release source (the GitLab project has tags, no release tarballs). See compile/libxslt/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/xsl/PROVENANCE.md.

netsnmp.$comment: For ext/snmp (mode: shared, 2026-09-23). Moved here from plannedLibraries (was keyed net-snmp; renamed to match compile/netsnmp and its Makefile target). libnetsnmp only: no agent, no apps, no MIB files installed, no Perl/Python. OpenSSL (the vendored libopenssl) for SNMPv3 SHA/AES. The GitHub tag archive is used: it ships a pre-generated configure. Tags include pre-releases (v5.10.preN) -- do not adopt those. See compile/netsnmp/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/snmp/PROVENANCE.md.

icu.$comment: For ext/intl (mode: shared, 2026-09-23). Moved here from plannedLibraries (was keyed ICU; renamed to match compile/icu and its Makefile target). Cross-compiled against a native build of itself (--with-cross-build) whose tools generate the data. libicuuc/libicui18n/libicuio only, static data packaging: the full data (~32 MB) is compiled into libicudata.a (the native icudt<major>l.dat turned into C by genccode) and linked into intl.so -- decided 2026-09-23, rather than a separate .dat loaded at runtime. configure has no emscripten host fragment (config/mh-unknown fails on purpose), so mh-linux is copied over it. Release tags are release-<version> for 78.x. compile/Makefile's FIREBIRD_ICU_VERSION (ICU headers for Firebird's build) is a separate, hardcoded pin. See compile/icu/Dockerfile and compile/extensions/intl/PROVENANCE.md.

libcxx.$comment: The C++ runtime (libc++, libc++abi, libunwind) as its own vendorLib, for C++ mode:shared extensions with no other vendored library to carry it (rar, 2026-09-23). Not downloaded: relocatable builds from the pinned emsdk (embuilder --pic, *-legacyexcept variants), so its version is the emsdk version (compile/base-image/Dockerfile) and moves only with it. The core has no C++ runtime; see compile/libcxx/Dockerfile and compile/firebird/Dockerfile.

anydoc.$comment: hosmelq/ext-anydoc (Packagist, extension name anydoc): PHP bindings for Firecrawl anydoc (documents to Markdown), in Rust via ext-php-rs. Built as a wasm32-unknown-emscripten staticlib on a pinned Rust nightly (-Zbuild-std, panic=abort, PIC) inside the compile-extension image, then linked into a thin phpize wrapper (compile/extensions/anydoc). Its version is the ext-anydoc tag, which matches the embedded anydoc crate version. See compile/anydoc/Dockerfile.

simdjson.$comment: For ext/jsonk (CLAUDE.md's jsonk decision) -- decode engine. Not built via a compile/lib*/Dockerfile+Makefile target like every other entry here: it ships as a single-header amalgamation (simdjson.h + simdjson.cpp) fetched as GitHub release assets straight into ext/jsonk/vendor/simdjson/ by compile/php/Dockerfile itself (no build step of its own), same layout php-jsonk's own vendor/build/stage.sh uses for a native dev build. Listed here anyway so getMatrixVersion() has one place to resolve it from, matching matrix.json's own "latest = last versions[] entry" convention.

yyjson.$comment: For ext/jsonk (CLAUDE.md's jsonk decision) -- encode engine + schema-document reader. Same "vendored flat file, no Dockerfile/Makefile target" shape as simdjson above (yyjson.h + yyjson.c fetched directly from the tagged ref into ext/jsonk/vendor/yyjson/).

utf8proc.$comment: For ext/norm (php-kirigami/php-norm) -- Unicode NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD normalization via utf8proc_map(). Same "vendored flat files, no compile/lib*/Dockerfile+Makefile target" shape as simdjson/yyjson above: utf8proc.h/utf8proc.c/utf8proc_data.c are already flat files at the JuliaStrings/utf8proc repo root (utf8proc_data.c is a pre-generated Unicode data table, committed by the maintainers, #include'd by utf8proc.c itself -- never compiled as its own translation unit), fetched directly from the tagged ref straight into ext/norm/vendor/utf8proc/ by compile/php/Dockerfile, same layout php-norm's own vendor/build/stage.sh uses for a native dev build.

extensions.$comment: Ported from php-static-autobuilder's own matrix.json (https://github.com/ZmotriN/php-static-autobuilder), 2026-09-12, per CLAUDE.md decisions 24/28. Fields: builtin (part of php-src vs. a separate repo), mandatory, switch (the ./configure flag), dependencies (other extensions it needs), libraries (third-party libs it needs — the per-extension dependency list requested by the user, matching LIB_TARGETS_BY_EXTENSION in compile/cli.mjs conceptually, though the two aren't wired together yet and use different library-name spellings: this section keeps php-static-autobuilder's own names verbatim, e.g. 'zlib'/'libpng'/'openssl', not this repo's 'libz'/'libpng16'/'libopenssl'). Windows-only extensions (win32std, winbinder, wcli, win32ps, win32service, com_dotnet) were dropped entirely, not carried over — they don't apply to a WASM/Node target. Data only: none of this is wired into compile/php/Dockerfile or cli.mjs's IMPLEMENTED_EXTENSIONS yet, most of these 103 extensions aren't buildable here at all today (see config.yaml's long 'off' list and CLAUDE.md's Context section for what's actually wired).

curl.note: Reconciled 2026-09-12 against this repo's actual compile/php/Dockerfile (php-static-autobuilder used different library names/deps for this extension).

openssl.note: Reconciled 2026-09-12 against this repo's actual compile/php/Dockerfile (php-static-autobuilder used different library names/deps for this extension).

bz2.note: Added 2026-09-17 as mode: static, prompted by this very entry's own long-standing 'dependencies: [bz2]' below on phar (ported from php-static-autobuilder, unacted-on until the user pointed it out): phar's util.c/phar_object.c gate .tar.bz2 support behind a plain `#if HAVE_BZ2` compiled-time check that only becomes true when ext/bz2 is built into the SAME configure invocation -- no way to give phar bzip2 support without also compiling ext/bz2's own bzcompress()/bzdecompress() into the static core (both come from the same config.m4 block). First tried as mode: shared (this matrix's own 'libbz2' entry above, genuinely needing a new vendored C library, unlike posix/ftp/dba's decisions 42/48/49) and built/smoke-tested successfully as a real @kirigami/phpext-bz2 package -- along the way, found and fixed a real libtool bug worth keeping on record for any future PHP_CHECK_LIBRARY-style (not pkg-config-based) mode:shared extension: config.m4's own `PHP_CHECK_LIBRARY([bz2], ...)` + `PHP_ADD_LIBRARY_WITH_PATH(...)` generates a `-L... -lbz2` link flag libtool's shared-link mode can't resolve against a static-only archive with no `.la` sidecar (warns 'no real file for library -lbz2', silently falls back to a static-only module, never produces the `.so`) -- fixed by dropping that block and letting this pipeline's generic vendorLib mechanism (--extra-ldflags -> EMCC_STATIC_ARCHIVES -> a patched libtool --whole-archive injection) supply the archive directly, the same underlying mechanism sodium's own config.m4 already (if less visibly) relies on. Abandoned that path once the phar dependency made static the better fit (registering the same extension both ways would be redundant) -- the shared package/compile/extensions/bz2/ vendor tree was removed again.

zip.note: Reconciled 2026-09-12 against this repo's actual compile/php/Dockerfile (php-static-autobuilder used different library names/deps for this extension).

gd.note: Reconciled 2026-09-12 against this repo's actual compile/php/Dockerfile (php-static-autobuilder used different library names/deps for this extension).

gettext.note: Added 2026-09-17 (next batch after bz2). No library to vendor, unlike this entry's inherited php-static-autobuilder 'libintl' note (a real dependency on Windows/glibc-less targets) -- confirmed by a real test compile that Emscripten's own musl libc already ships <libintl.h> plus no-op bindtextdomain/gettext/ngettext/etc. implementations directly in libc (musl has no real i18n message-catalog support, so these are stubs that just hand back the input string unchanged), and a trivial C program calling them links cleanly against kirigami-php-wasm:base with zero extra -l flags. config.m4's own DIR-detection loop (`test -r $i/include/libintl.h`) still needs a real filesystem path though, so compile/php/Dockerfile points `--with-gettext=` straight at `$(em-config CACHE)/sysroot` rather than vendoring a copy.

gmp.note: Added 2026-09-17 (next batch after bz2). pcntl.note: Tried 2026-09-16 (CLAUDE.md decision 48's batch), deliberately abandoned -- not just left mode: off, removed from config.yaml and compile/extensions/ entirely (same treatment as ext/cmark, decision 40). Hit a real cross-compile false positive first (HAVE_GETCPUID wrongly detected, pulling in Solaris's <sys/processor.h> -- fixed with a direct edit to the vendored pcntl.c, `&& !defined(__EMSCRIPTEN__)` on that one guard), then a second build failure not worth chasing. More fundamentally: its entire feature set (fork(), waitpid(), inter-process signals) has no real equivalent in a single-instance WASM VM with no real OS process model -- even a successful build would ship functions that silently do nothing useful or fail unpredictably, unlike shmop/sysvshm/sysvmsg/sysvsem which at least have a plausible path to real behavior. `disabled: true` marks this as "tried and rejected", not "not yet attempted" -- don't re-attempt without a real reason to revisit that conclusion.

yaml.$comment: Sourced from the extension's own GitHub repo/tags, not pecl.php.net's package archive — PECL's own listing lags behind (CLAUDE.md decision 34: 'often bien plus a jour' on GitHub).

apcu.note: On va probablement la mettre dans le core si la mémoire persiste dans la vm de php-wasm -- being tried now: added to config.yaml as mode: static (CLAUDE.md's jsonk/apcu decision). Verified 2026-09-16 against apcu's real config.m4: igbinary (removed from "dependencies" above, that field doesn't exist on this entry anymore) is only an optional faster serializer it detects at runtime, not a hard PHP_ADD_EXTENSION_DEP -- the field carried over from php-static-autobuilder's matrix.json was wrong. Its rwlock/mutex pthread capability probes use AC_RUN_IFELSE but already supply a real cross-compiling action (assume yes, same as native) -- unlike ext/cmark's AC_TRY_RUN (CLAUDE.md decision 34), no patch needed there. Not yet build-tested: whether Emscripten's non-`-pthread` build actually resolves the pthread_mutex*/pthread_rwlock* symbols APCu's own "yes" assumption links against is unconfirmed.

rar.$comment: cataphract/php-rar (PECL rar, published for PIE as cataphract/rar), mode: shared (2026-09-23). Read-only RAR support (RAR 1.5 to RAR5, multi-volume, encrypted) through the unrar source bundled in the extension itself (C++), so its only vendorLib is libcxx. Vendored under compile/extensions/rar from the GitHub tag, see its PROVENANCE.md.

imagick.note: Not present in php-static-autobuilder's own matrix (Windows php builder never added it) — added 2026-09-12 since this repo does support it (compile/php/Dockerfile WITH_IMAGICK block). Was tracking the unpinned 'master' branch directly (compile/php/Dockerfile's own IMAGICK_BRANCH="master" for PHP 8.x) until a real, user-noticed bug: php_imagick.h ships `#define PHP_IMAGICK_VERSION "@PACKAGE_VERSION@"` literally (its own comment: "deliberately left as PACKAGE_VERSION in source code") — a placeholder only ever substituted by PECL's own packaging tool (`pecl package`, reading package.xml) at release-tarball-build time, which this pipeline's plain `git clone`/tag-tarball fetch never runs, so phpinfo() displayed the raw, unsubstituted string. Fixed 2026-09-16 by pinning to the real latest tag (3.8.1) instead of floating on master (also makes the build reproducible, closing the same class of gap decision 11 already flagged for oniguruma) and sed-replacing @PACKAGE_VERSION@ with that same pinned version in compile/php/Dockerfile right after fetching.

mdhtml.$comment: php-kirigami/php-mdhtml -- our own CommonMark+GFM extension (cmark-gfm-based), replacing ext/cmark as the core, static-mode markdown renderer (CLAUDE.md decision 37; see extensions.cmark's own 'ABANDONED' note). config.m4 uses PHP_ARG_WITH (--with-mdhtml[=DIR]), same shape as ext/cmark's own --with-cmark.

jsonk.$comment: php-kirigami/php-jsonk (the user's own project) -- fast JSON encode/decode + JSON Schema validation, built on vendored simdjson (decode)+yyjson (encode/schema-doc reads), see matrix.json's own "simdjson"/"yyjson" entries above. Has a HARD zend_module_dep on "json" and "pcre" -- it can't load without ext/json already loaded, so this build doesn't (and can't) disable ext/json: php-src's own ext/json/config.m4 takes no PHP_ARG_ENABLE at all in PHP 8.5, there is no --disable-json flag to begin with. "Replacing json" (as requested) is done by flipping jsonk's own "jsonk.replace_json_functions" ini default from its upstream "0" to "1" for this build (a one-line sed via /root/replace.sh in compile/php/Dockerfile, not a patches/jsonk/*.patch file -- too small a literal-string change to warrant one). Not yet build-tested: the first C++ extension in this pipeline (config.m4's PHP_REQUIRE_CXX/-std=c++17), though JSPI mode's existing -fwasm-exceptions flag (decision 6) means real C++ exceptions are already supported if simdjson's amalgamation ever needs them (jsonk_decode.cpp itself only uses simdjson's non-throwing .get() API).

navicat.$comment: php-kirigami/php-navicat (the user's own project) -- native client for Navicat Premium's HTTP-tunnel protocol (ntunnel_mysql.php), reverse-engineered from Navicat's own server scripts. config.m4 uses PHP_ARG_WITH (--with-navicat[=DIR]), reusing the libcurl already linked in via the WITH_CURL block for the static build -- no separate .emcc-php-wasm-sources entry needed, libcurl.a is already appended there.

igbinary.$comment: igbinary/igbinary -- faster binary serializer, no external lib. Its own config.m4 auto-detects apcu (checks for ext/apcu/apc_serializer.h at configure time) and registers itself as an APCu serializer when found -- this build also flips apcu's own "apc.serializer" ini default from "php" to "igbinary" (CLAUDE.md decision 45's follow-up, only when WITH_IGBINARY=yes).

norm.$comment: php-kirigami/php-norm (the user's own project) -- native Normalizer class + normalizer_normalize()/normalizer_is_normalized() functions, wrapping vendored utf8proc (see matrix.json's own "utf8proc" library entry above), same 'vendored flat source files, no compile/lib*/Dockerfile' shape as ext/jsonk's simdjson/yyjson (utf8proc.c is compiled directly into ext/norm's own object files -- no separate .a, no .emcc-php-wasm-sources entry needed). Only registers its Normalizer class/normalizer_*() functions if intl (or anything else) hasn't already provided them (zend_hash_str_exists guards in PHP_MINIT_FUNCTION(norm), ZEND_MOD_OPTIONAL("intl") purely for MINIT ordering) -- safe to always build in as mode: static regardless of intl's own state.

scanmeqr.$comment: crazy-goat/qrcode-ext (Packagist, PIE extension name scanmeqr): the native QR encoder behind crazy-goat/scanmephp. mode: shared (2026-09-23). Its C++20 core is bundled in the package (no external library), so its only vendorLib is libcxx. Keyed by the extension name, which is also the config.yaml key and the npm package name (@kirigami/phpext-scanmeqr). Vendored under compile/extensions/scanmeqr from the GitHub tag, see its PROVENANCE.md.

fastchart.$comment: iliaal/fastchart (Packagist, PIE extension name fastchart): chart rendering to SVG/PNG/JPEG/WebP. mode: shared (2026-09-23). Bundles plutovg/plutosvg/qrcodegen; links freetype, libpng16, libjpeg, libwebp, libz (the gd codec libs). Vendored under compile/extensions/fastchart from the GitHub tag, see its PROVENANCE.md.

anydoc.$comment: hosmelq/ext-anydoc, mode: shared (2026-09-23): the first Rust extension. The Rust crate itself is built as the anydoc library (matrix libraries.anydoc, compile/anydoc/Dockerfile); compile/extensions/anydoc is only the phpize wrapper.

plannedLibraries.$comment: Requested 2026-09-12: build out Dockerfiles for (ideally) every library + extension php-static-autobuilder's own matrix.json covers (CLAUDE.md decision 24). This section records real, gh-api-verified upstream sources + currently-latest versions for the ones not yet wired into a compile/<lib>/Dockerfile — data-entry done, Dockerfiles not written/tested yet. Excludes Windows-only libraries from php-static-autobuilder's list that don't apply to a WASM/Linux cross-compile (pthread-win32, wineditline, dirent, fbclient's nocrt Windows build). A few repos could not be auto-verified (no matching release/tag found via the GitHub API in one pass) and are marked 'checkUrl: manual' instead of a repo — needs a human/deeper look, not a confirmed gap.

zlib.note: We already vendor zlib as 'libz' (zlib.net tarball, tested/working) — this is just recording the alternate GitHub-mirror source php-static-autobuilder uses, not a second copy to build.
